subject: Temporary headroom extension + billing smoothing request
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@brightbay.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbay.com, kevin.legal@brightbay.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — short-term headroom and smoothing of charges

Hi David,

We're ramping a paid marketing push on Oct 15 that will spike our inference usage for ~3 weeks. Our platform team estimates we could be 2.5–3x our usual daily token consumption for ~21 days. Before we flip the campaign on, procurement asked me to check if Redwood can:  

- provision a temporary headroom increase (rate-limit/quota bump) for the campaign window, and
- provide a billing smoothing for the expected overrun — ideally amortized across the next 1–2 invoices rather than a single oversized charge.

We want to avoid abrupt rate throttles mid-campaign and also keep our finance team from getting a surprise one-off invoice.

Can you advise what temporary uplift options you have and whether you can offer an amortized reconciliation for the overage? We can share updated usage forecast (attached) and our campaign dates. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Park
Director of Growth, BrightBay Retail
emily@brightbay.com

Attachment: usage_forecast_Q4.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@brightbay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short-term headroom and smoothing of charges

Hi Emily — thanks for the heads up and for the forecast file.

We can absolutely provision a temporary headroom increase for the campaign window. To avoid surprises on both sides, we usually handle these requests with a provisional uplift and an overrun reconciliation. A straightforward option we can offer today:

- Temporary quota increase for the campaign window (we can lock dates: Oct 15–Nov 5).
- Overrun usage billed at list rate + a one-time uplift (example: 15% on overrun tokens) and we can amortize that over the next two invoices so you don't get a single large spike.

I want to validate internal approval on the exact surcharge and confirm there are no contractual blockers for amortization. Ben/Marissa — can you confirm if we can present a 15% uplift on overrun with amortization across two invoices? Also throwing to Finance for confirmation on invoicing cadence — @Monica, are you ok with splitting the overrun reconciliation across the following two billing cycles if we present this as a provisional amendment?

Emily — I attached a one-page provisional amendment (pdf) that shows dates, capped uplift, and proposed amortization language. If that's acceptable in principle, I'll create a DocuSign and route for signatures today so we can lock the capacity before Oct 15.

Best,
David
David Kim
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: provisional-amendment-20261007.pdf (pdf, 52KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick ask — short-term headroom and smoothing of charges

Thumbs up on making this low-friction for the customer, with a couple guardrails. My suggested terms to offer BrightBay:

- Temporary headroom: increase token throughput up to 3x baseline for Oct 15–Nov 5. If their baseline is unclear, we should peg it to the trailing 30d average and multiply by 3.
- Cap the uplift commitment: chargeable overrun only for usage above 3x baseline; up to that cap it's covered by the temporary headroom.
- Overrun surcharge: 12% on tokens above the cap (discounted from your proposed 15%).
- Billing smoothing: amortize the overrun (surcharge + overrun usage) across the next two invoices — Finance to split evenly.
- One-time setup/onboarding fee waived for campaign (to keep momentum).

Monica — confirm the two-invoice split is operationally OK and whether we need a PO amendment or just a signed provisional amendment. If we need a PO, request that procurement send it to billing@redwood.com.

If that's acceptable, David you can present this as our formal offer. Keeps it customer-friendly, protects us with a cap, and lets us avoid a surprise invoice.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@brightbay.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbay.com, kevin.legal@brightbay.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short-term headroom and smoothing of charges

Hi Emily — quick update and proposed terms based on internal review. Apologies for the short email; wanted to lock this before the weekend.

Proposal (BrightBay Retail) — temporary headroom and billing smoothing
- Window: Oct 15, 2026 00:00 PT — Nov 5, 2026 23:59 PT
- Headroom: up to 3x your trailing 30d average daily token consumption (we'll sync on baseline number).
- Overrun handling: any usage above the 3x cap will be billed at list rate + 12% surcharge.
- Billing smoothing: surcharge + billed overrun will be amortized across your next two invoices (split evenly).
- Setup fee: waived for this campaign.

Next steps: if this looks good, I'll generate a provisional amendment and route via DocuSign (link included). If procurement prefers a PO before we enable the uplift, send it to billing@redwood.com and we'll hold the headroom until it's processed.

DocuSign (provisional amendment): https://www.docusign.net/temporary-amendment/BB-4321
HubSpot for the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/BB-4321

Emily — let me know if procurement needs any additional language. If you're good, I'll start the signature flow and enable the uplift on Oct 14 EOD to give your team time to validate.

Thanks,
David Kim
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
